## Natural history notes

A small flower fly characterized by its slender body, large reddish eyes, and yellow-and-black patterned abdomen with dark side margins that help give it a neatly bordered appearance. In Florida, it is common in gardens, fields, roadsides, parks, forest edges, wetlands, and other sunny habitats with abundant flowers and low vegetation. Adults visit flowers for nectar and pollen, while the larvae prey on aphids and other small soft-bodied insects, making this species a beneficial natural enemy in gardens and natural areas.
